target.title: fix(groq): keep default Llama agent turns within TPM limit
target.body:
Closes #104783

AI-assisted with Codex. I reviewed the implementation and the live proof.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running a local agent with `groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile` could receive an immediate HTTP 413 for even a one-word prompt on Groq's 12,000 TPM base tier. The default agent request combined the model's full 32,768-token output capability with the normal prompt and tool schemas, making the request too large before generation began.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Groq plugin now keeps the model's 32,768-token output capability metadata while applying a separate 1,024-token default request budget. Normal implicit-budget requests remain tool-capable; only a specifically matched Groq HTTP 413 `Request too large` TPM rejection is retried once without tool fields. Explicit max-token overrides skip this recovery policy. The change stays provider- and model-scoped instead of changing shared OpenAI-compatible transport behavior or hard-coding an account's TPM tier as the model capability.

## User Impact

Default local-agent turns with `groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile` can complete on Groq's base tier instead of failing before generation. Higher-limit organizations retain the normal tool-capable first request, while affected base-tier requests recover transparently. Other Groq models and explicitly budgeted requests are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before, on current `main`, the exact isolated local-agent flow returned HTTP 413: Groq reported `Limit 12000, Requested 61830` for the one-word prompt `你好`.
- After, the same default command first received the narrowly matched HTTP 413, immediately retried without tool fields, and returned HTTP 200 in the same agent attempt. Groq reported 10,071 input tokens and 452 output tokens (10,523 total).
- An explicit 128-token budget with the `session_status` tool also returned HTTP 200. Groq reported 8,860 input tokens and 6 output tokens (8,866 total), and the live system-prompt report retained `session_status`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/groq` — 4 tests passed, including normal tool retention, exact 413 recovery, explicit-budget preservation, and non-recovery for unrelated 400/401/413-context/429 errors.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/groq/index.ts extensions/groq/index.test.ts extensions/groq/openclaw.plugin.json` — clean.
- `git diff --check` — clean.

Hosted local validation was unavailable on this machine: Blacksmith Testbox was not installed, and direct AWS Crabbox had no usable instance credentials. The focused local fallback and live provider proof above completed successfully; GitHub CI remains the broad validation gate.

target.title: fix(config): reject zero-value resetArchiveRetention to prevent silent data loss
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Configuring `session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention: "0h"` (or any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to zero) is silently accepted by Zod config validation. `parseDurationMs("0h")` returns `0` without throwing, so the `superRefine` passes the value. `resolveResetArchiveRetentionMs` returns `0ms` with no guard, and cleanup computes `cutoff = now - 0 = now`, matching all reset transcript archives for immediate deletion.

## Changes

**Schema gate (prevention)**: Added `ms <= 0` guard in `superRefine` to reject any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to ≤ 0 at config validation time. The documented disable sentinel (`false`) is unaffected.

**Doctor migration (upgrade safety)**: Added a registered legacy rule + migration in the existing session maintenance migration file that uses `parseDurationMs` (same `{ defaultUnit: "d" }` options as schema) in both detection and repair paths. This covers all parser-equivalent zero representations — `"0"`, `"0h"`, `"0d"`, `"0ms"`, `"0s"`, `"0m"`, `"0.0h"`, `"0h0m"`, `"0h0m0s"`, etc. The migration removes only values that parse to ≤ 0 so the documented pruneAfter default applies; positive durations, `false`, and unparseable strings are preserved.

### Files changed (4 files, +248/-3)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/zod-schema.session.ts` | +14/-3: reject zero-duration in superRefine |
| `src/config/zod-schema.session-maintenance-extensions.test.ts` | +27: schema regression cases |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.ts` | +49: parser-backed rule + migration spec |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.test.ts` | +155: 16 focused tests |

## Evidence

### All tests passing

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/zod-schema.session-maintenance-extensions.test.ts
Tests  13 passed (13)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.test.ts
Tests  16 passed (16)
```

### Before fix: schema gate rejects zero values

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"resetArchiveRetention":"0h"}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{
  "valid": false,
  "path": "/tmp/cfg.json5",
  "issues": [
    {
      "path": "session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention",
      "message": "duration must be positive (use ms, s, m, h, d), e.g. 30d"
    }
  ]
}
```

### After fix: positive intervals still accepted

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"resetArchiveRetention":"30d"}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/cfg.json5","warnings":[]}
```

### After fix: `false` (documented disable) unaffected

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"resetArchiveRetention":false}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/cfg.json5","warnings":[]}
```

### Doctor detection → repair

Doctor detects via parser-backed rule:

```
session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention is a zero duration — this
causes immediate deletion of all reset transcript archives. Run
"openclaw doctor --fix" to remove it so the documented pruneAfter
default applies.
```

Doctor repairs:

```
Removed session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention "0h" (zero duration);
documented pruneAfter default applies.
```

### Unparseable values preserved for schema diagnostic

`"abc"`, `""` — not matched by doctor rule, not removed by migration. Schema diagnostic handles these.

### Diff whitespace checks

`git diff --check` passed.

- **Not tested / proof gaps**: None.

target.title: fix(ai): guard payload-less media blocks from erasing tool-result text
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A tool-result content block labeled `image` or `audio` with no recognizable payload causes the entire tool output to be replaced by `"(see attached image)"` — the phantom media placeholder tells the model media was attached when nothing was sent.
- **Problem**: `extractToolResultBlockText` returns `undefined` for every media-typed block regardless of payload, and `describeToolResultMediaPlaceholder` advertises media from payload-less husks. When a tool result contains only payload-less media blocks (no text blocks), the output degrades to `"(see attached image)"`.
- **Solution**: Add `hasMediaPayload()` and `hasInlineMediaData()` predicates. Use them in `describeToolResultMediaPlaceholder` and `extractToolResultBlockText` to skip/flag payload-less blocks instead of producing phantom media placeholders. Guard all provider emitters against emitting empty image blocks.
- **What changed**:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/tool-result-text.ts` — shared helpers (hasMediaPayload, hasInlineMediaData, fixed placeholder fallback)
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/tool-result-text.test.ts` — 18 tests
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` — emitter guard
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.ts` — emitter guard
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/mistral.ts` — emitter guard
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` — emitter guard
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.ts` — emitter guard
  - `src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.ts` — transport emitter guard
  - `src/agents/openai-transport-stream.ts` — transport emitter guard
- **What did NOT change**: Session persistence, database schema, config format, public API types

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix

## Scope

- [x] API / contracts

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #104721
- Related #100795 (broader approach — same root cause, this PR is a focused subset)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Issue #104721 reports that all tool results return `"(see attached image)"` literal placeholder text instead of actual output across deepseek-v4-flash and gpt-5.5 models. The root cause is that `describeToolResultMediaPlaceholder` and `extractToolResultBlockText` in the shared `tool-result-text.ts` treat every media-typed content block as genuine media, even when it carries no payload. A payload-less media block (from session corruption, plugin bugs, or older sessions) causes the tool result text to vanish and be replaced with a media placeholder.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Tool results with payload-less media blocks no longer degrade to phantom media placeholders
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 22, branch `fix/media-payload-guard-104721`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
pnpm test packages/ai/src/providers/tool-result-text.test.ts
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ pnpm test packages/ai/src/providers/tool-result-text.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  18 passed (18)

$ pnpm test packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  68 passed (68)

$ pnpm test packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  43 passed (43)
```

**Matrix-style evidence (before vs after)**:

| Scenario | Input | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Phantom image replaces output | `[{type:"image"}]` (no data) | `extractToolResultText` → `""` → output becomes `"(see attached image)"` | `extractToolResultText` → `"[image omitted: missing payload]"` |
| Phantom audio replaces output | `[{type:"audio"}]` (no data) | Same, `"(see attached audio)"` | `"[audio omitted: missing payload]"` |
| Text + phantom image | `[{type:"text",text:"real output"},{type:"image"}]` | `"real output"` (text preserved) but emitter sends empty image block | `"real output"` + emitter skips empty image |
| Genuine image (unchanged) | `[{type:"image",data:"img"}]` | `undefined` (media path) / `"(see attached image)"` | Same ✅ |
| Text block with image mime | `[{type:"text",text:"hello",mimeType:"image/png"}]` | False image detection → `"(see attached image)"` | No false detection → `undefined` ✅ |
| hasInlineMediaData | `{type:"image",data:"img"}` | N/A (new function) | `true` ✅ |
| hasInlineMediaData | `{type:"image"}` (no data) | N/A (new function) | `false` ✅ |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. `extractToolResultText` returns `"[image omitted: missing payload]"` for payload-less image-only content instead of empty string
  2. `describeToolResultMediaPlaceholder` returns `undefined` for payload-less media blocks instead of `"(see attached image)"`
  3. Text blocks with image-like mime metadata no longer trigger false image detection
  4. Mixed text + payload-less-image content correctly returns the text
  5. Provider-native emitters skip payload-less image blocks instead of emitting empty image URLs / base64 data
- What was not tested: Live end-to-end provider API calls (guarded by the same pattern in converters + unit tests)

- **Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**
  - ✅ Auth guard: N/A — no permission/policy changes
  - ✅ Enum completeness: `hasMediaPayload` covers all canonical wire shapes (data, url, file_id, image_url string/object, source.data/url, input_audio, audio); `hasInlineMediaData` covers inline base64
  - ✅ Path coverage: Shared helpers (`describeToolResultMediaPlaceholder`, `extractToolResultBlockText`) + all 5 provider emitters + 2 transport streams use the same guards
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: Payload-less media blocks get a fixed placeholder text, not JSON stringification (which could leak nested payload-shaped fields)

## Root Cause

Payload-less media-typed content blocks (e.g. `{ type: "image", mimeType: "image/png" }` without `data`) suppress text extraction and advertise phantom media. The shared functions in `packages/ai/src/providers/tool-result-text.ts` trusted the type label alone — no payload verification existed.

## Regression Test Plan

All 18 existing + new tests pass. Broader provider tests (anthropic 68, openai-completions 43, google-shared 12) also pass unchanged.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Tool results with payload-less media blocks show `"[image omitted: missing payload]"` instead of `"(see attached image)"`
- All other behavior unchanged

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — the shared `tool-result-text.ts` is the correct boundary for text extraction; all provider emitters also need the inline-data guard to prevent invalid API payloads
- **Refactor needed**: No — targeted 9-file change with consistent pattern across all emitters
- **Alternative considered**: Shared-helper-only approach (commit 1) — fixed text extraction but didn't prevent emitters from sending empty image blocks. Expanded to cover emitters after ClawSweeper review (commit 2)

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: A payload-less media block from a genuine source (e.g. plugin that intentionally sends empty media) now renders as `"[image omitted: missing payload]"` text instead of `"(see attached image)"`. This is strictly better — the model gets a readable explanation rather than a misleading "image was attached" message.

**Mitigation**: Backward compatible for genuine media (blocks with `data`/`url`/`file_id` payloads are unaffected). The change only affects payload-less blocks that were already broken (producing incorrect placeholder text).

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

---

Fixes #104721

target.title: fix(browser): check own profile entries for profile operations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser profile names are user-controlled config keys. Inherited object properties such as `constructor` and `prototype` were treated as real profile entries in several create, delete, projection, hot-reload, and gateway patch paths. A valid profile with one of those names could therefore be rejected, omitted, or fail to round-trip.

Live route testing also exposed an adjacent deletion failure: when `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` or `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` placed Browser state outside the OS home/temp roots, deleting a launched profile returned HTTP 500 because the trash helper rejected Browser's own configured state directory.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Use own-property checks at every Browser profile lookup boundary.
- Preserve valid top-level profile keys while continuing to strip nested prototype-pollution keys from untrusted config patches.
- Keep profile listing and hot reload consistent with persisted config.
- Authorize trash moves only from Browser's owned `<config>/browser` subtree. Existing realpath, symlink-escape, target-identity, and trash-destination checks remain in force; the wider config directory is not authorized.

## User Impact

Profiles named `constructor` or `prototype` can be created, listed, hot-reloaded, patched, and deleted normally. Custom state directories outside the home directory work without granting Browser deletion authority over unrelated config or filesystem paths.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `194d41eab680c1964c70087a60e03df607470878`
- Exact GitHub CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29032054298 - passed.
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox: lease `cbx_7b2824bafef4`, run `run_231cff1f9ccb`; public networking, no Tailscale, no instance profile, IMDSv2 IAM endpoint 404, exact head verified, Node 24.15 / pnpm 11.2.2; 180 focused tests passed. Lease released.
- Native `OPENCLAW_TESTBOX=1 scripts/pr prepare-run 101694` - passed at the exact PR head.
- Fresh autoreview at the exact head - clean, confidence 0.91.
- Real Express route proof: create and delete `constructor` through `POST /profiles/create` and `DELETE /profiles/constructor`; persistence round-tripped and `Object.prototype` remained unchanged.
- Real Gateway RPC proof: `config.patch` created and removed the profile while nested `constructor` / `prototype` payload keys remained stripped.
- Custom-state route proof: launched/stopped profile deletion under a configured state directory outside home/temp succeeds; unrelated config subtrees, root config authority, and symlink escapes remain rejected.

Live Dev Gateway + OpenAI agent + Browser proof will be added before merge; it is intentionally not claimed by the current evidence.

### 2026-07-12 follow-up: exact-head local proof

- Exact PR head verified locally: `ca0e4b3eff432c1c77cf5ae1810712c9e7570668`.
- Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/profiles-service.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.hot-reload-profiles.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.list-profiles.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/trash.test.ts src/config/merge-patch.proto-pollution.test.ts src/gateway/server.config-patch.test.ts`.
- Result: passed 3 Vitest shards in 104.64s; 7 focused files passed; 139 tests passed.
- Coverage from the focused files: Browser profile own-entry create/list/hot-reload paths, prototype-like profile keys, trash authorization for Browser-owned state, nested prototype-pollution stripping in config merge patches, and Gateway `config.patch` behavior.
- This is exact-head local controlled proof. No live Dev Gateway, external provider, or browser UI session was exercised in this follow-up.

## Proof

- Exact head tested: `c6055930d28aa0ecbe469406b0cdb60244a64526`

target.title: fix(openai): redact token refresh error response body
target.body:
﻿## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Codex OAuth token refresh reads the full error response body via `response.text()` on failed requests with no size limit and no redaction. Secrets in error responses (e.g. `refresh_token` in `error_description`) are exposed in the error message.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the unbounded `response.text()` with `extractProviderErrorDetail` ? the canonical bounded provider error helper ? so error body consumption is capped at 16 KiB and sensitive values are redacted.

Matches the merged Chutes OAuth fix ([#103569](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103569)): `readResponseTextLimited` ? `assertOkOrThrowProviderError`, with secret redaction tests.

## User Impact

**Before:** unbounded error body read, secrets in error responses logged
**After:** bounded at 16 KiB via `extractProviderErrorDetail`, secrets redacted

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** OpenAI OAuth token refresh/authorization failures read unbounded response bodies and embed raw provider error text; the fix caps error body reads at 16 KiB and redacts sensitive values (refresh_token, access_token) from returned failure messages.

**Real environment tested:** Windows 11, Node.js v24.18.0, openclaw commit `8201b1c3` on branch `fix/openai-oauth-refresh-error-body`.

**Steps run after the patch:**
```
// Live loopback proof ? exercises extractProviderErrorDetail against real HTTP server
node --import tsx scripts/proof/openai-oauth-refresh-live.mts

// Full-chain regression tests ? exercises postTokenForm ? readResponseWithLimit ? extractProviderErrorDetail
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.test.ts
```

**Evidence after fix:**
```
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof/openai-oauth-refresh-live.mts

=== #103578 bounded OAuth error proof ===

Case 1 ? secret redacted from error body: PASS
Case 2 ? oversized body bounded: PASS
Case 3 ? normal body preserved: PASS

OVERALL: ALL PASSED
```

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)
```

**Observed result after fix:** The loopback proof exercises `extractProviderErrorDetail` against a real HTTP server with realistic OAuth error responses containing `refresh_token` and `access_token` fields ? secret values are redacted, oversized bodies are capped at 16 KiB, and normal error text is preserved. The regression tests exercise the full production `postTokenForm` ? `readResponseWithLimit` ? `refreshAccessToken`/`exchangeAuthorizationCode` chain via mocked SSRF, confirming both callers return bounded, redacted failure messages.

**What was not tested:** A live OAuth flow against the real `auth.openai.com` endpoint could not be executed because it requires a valid OpenAI OAuth client_id/client_secret pair (not available to external contributors). The loopback proof exercises the same production `extractProviderErrorDetail` function with realistic error payloads; the runtime tests exercise the same `postTokenForm` production path with bounded response reading and the same caller-level redaction logic.

target.title: Instrument native hook relay fan-out
target.body:
## Summary
- add per-registration native hook relay metrics for command requests and real invocations
- log aggregate relay summaries at unregister with event counts, total/max duration, and no-local-work command requests
- warn on slow native hook relay invocations (>=250ms) with relay/session/tool context

## What Problem This Solves
Operators observed short, high-CPU bursts from `openclaw-hooks` workers during normal Telegram/Codex activity. Source inspection points at Codex native hook relay fan-out as a likely hot path: the Codex harness can register native events such as `pre_tool_use`, `post_tool_use`, `permission_request`, and `before_agent_finalize`; when local work exists, those events cross a process boundary through `openclaw hooks relay`.

The important next step is observability, not behavior change. This PR adds low-noise aggregate metrics around the native hook relay path so operators can confirm which relay events are requested, which ones actually invoke OpenClaw work, how long they take, and whether no-local-work requests are still contributing to fan-out.

This PR does not change relay behavior, approval semantics, hook policy, or gateway configuration.

## Evidence
Redacted live host observations from the OpenClaw hook-burst investigation:

- 2026-07-06 hook-cost audit: short-lived `openclaw-hooks` workers were observed around 145-175% CPU during normal Telegram/OpenClaw use, with CPU temperature near 97C in one snapshot. A later audit snapshot reproduced one `openclaw-hooks` worker around 159% CPU while CPU temperature was 83.6C.
- Controlled local timing sample after a temporary operator-only runtime timing patch on OpenClaw 2026.6.11: 19 native relay invocations in roughly 40 seconds, including 10 `pre_tool_use` calls at 1-54ms and 9 `post_tool_use` calls at 0-1ms. No `>=250ms` slow relay lines appeared in that short sample, which suggests the burst problem is likely process fan-out/overlap rather than one slow handler.
- During that same sample, a short-lived `openclaw-hooks` worker was observed around 163% CPU and disappeared within seconds.
- 2026-07-06 post-restart memory watch: pre-restart gateway cgroup memory was about 2.5GB, gateway node RSS about 887MB, swap effectively full, and another short-lived `openclaw-hooks` burst hit about 166% CPU. Immediately after restart, another short-lived hook worker hit about 157% CPU during the first post-restart turn.
- 2026-07-06 workload checkpoint after starting a real Symphony/Codex review lane: gateway cgroup memory rose to about 7.0GB with 584 tasks while gateway node RSS stayed under about 1GB; two short-lived `openclaw-hooks` workers were observed around 162-163% CPU, with multiple Codex app-server workers active under the gateway cgroup. This points at child-process fan-out/worker overlap rather than a single gateway heap-only leak.
- 2026-07-08 follow-up inspection: gateway cgroup memory was about 5.6GB, cgroup peak about 9.1GB, 417 tasks, swap about 7.3GB/8GB used, 8 resident Codex app-server wrapper/native pairs, and a short-lived `openclaw-hooks` worker around 170% CPU / 340MB RSS while inspecting.

Source-level findings from the same investigation:

- The live config did not explicitly set `nativeHookRelay`; the Codex harness enabled native hook relay by default.
- `post_tool_use` and `before_agent_finalize` are locally gated by whether matching global hooks exist, but once local work exists, the relay still crosses a process boundary.
- The generic void-hook path runs matching hook work in parallel, so several short-lived relay processes can overlap during tool-heavy turns.

## Relation To #101099
#101099 was an earlier timing-instrumentation lane from the same investigation. This PR is the cleaner/narrower aggregate-metrics lane:

- #101099 focused on timing logs from an operator patch direction.
- #102241 adds source-level per-registration counters, no-local-work request counts, aggregate unregister summaries, and slow-invocation warnings in one relay file.

If maintainers prefer one observability shape, this PR should supersede or narrow #101099 rather than both landing independently.

## Verification
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`
- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-hook-relay.test.ts` (13/13)
- `TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d /tmp/openclaw-native-relay-test-XXXXXX) node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.test.ts` (80/80)

Note: the same relay test without isolated `TMPDIR` can see a live gateway native-hook bridge record in the shared OS temp dir and fail its PID-isolation expectation; isolating `TMPDIR` avoids that host-local interference.

target.title: fix(agents): keep subagent run ID mask from splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the subagent run-ID mask used in lifecycle log/error metadata could emit isolated UTF-16 surrogate halves when the run ID contains astral characters (e.g., emoji).

## Why This Change Was Made

`maskRunId` sliced its prefix/suffix with raw `String.prototype.slice`, which can bisect surrogate pairs. It now uses the repository's existing `sliceUtf16Safe` helper so the masked ID always falls on valid UTF-16 boundaries. The helper was also moved to module scope and exported so it can be unit-tested directly.

## User Impact

Subagent lifecycle warnings and error metadata remain well-formed when run IDs contain non-BMP characters.

## Evidence

- Moved `maskRunId` to module scope in `src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts` and exported it.
- Added regression tests in `src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts` covering ASCII masking and astral boundary cases.
- Existing lifecycle controller tests continue to pass.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Before the patch, a run ID like `"abc😀xxxxxxxxx"` produced `"abc\ud83d…\ude00xxxx"` (isolated surrogate halves). After the patch it returns `"abc…xxxx"`.
- **Real environment tested:** Local checkout of `fix/mask-runid-utf16` at `71f75fbfa526d0041851c3530662325cc35ac424`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { maskRunId } from "./src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts"; for (const v of ["run-1234567890", "abc😀" + "x".repeat(10), "x".repeat(10) + "😀abc", "a😀b", "short"]) console.log(JSON.stringify(maskRunId(v)));'
  ```
  And to verify the masked values survive a real disk round-trip without corrupting:
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { maskRunId } from "./src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts"; import { writeFileSync, readFileSync, mkdtempSync } from "node:fs"; import { tmpdir } from "node:os"; import { join } from "node:path"; const f = join(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "mr-")), "m.txt"); const samples = ["run-1234567890", "abc😀" + "x".repeat(10), "x".repeat(10) + "😀abc", "a😀b"]; const masked = samples.map(maskRunId); writeFileSync(f, masked.join("\n"), "utf8"); const r = readFileSync(f, "utf8"); console.log(r); console.log("round-trip ok:", r === masked.join("\n"));'
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```
  "run-…7890"
  "abc…xxxx"
  "xxxx…abc"
  "***"

  run-…7890
  abc…xxxx
  xxxx…abc
  ***
  round-trip ok: true
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** The regression test `does not split UTF-16 surrogate pairs at mask boundaries` passes, `encodeURIComponent` succeeds on every masked value, no isolated surrogates are emitted, and the joined masked values survive a disk write/read round-trip.
- **What was not tested:** No live subagent lifecycle failure path; change is a pure string-formatting helper.

_AI-assisted PR: changes and tests were generated with AI assistance and manually reviewed._

target.title: fix(diagnostics): derive heap thresholds from V8 heap size limit (#104631)
target.body:
Closes #104631

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running the gateway with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size` above the default (e.g. 8 GB on a 15 GB RAM host) receive false-positive `heap_threshold` critical memory pressure diagnostics as soon as `heapUsedBytes` reaches 2 GB, even when the V8 heap limit has 75%+ headroom and the system has abundant free memory.

This triggers unnecessary diagnostic events, log noise, and stability bundle writes, and can cause downstream monitoring or supervisor restart chains (the linked issue reports a gateway drain-and-restart sequence on the reporter's setup).

## Why This Change Was Made

The diagnostic memory classifier previously hardcoded heap pressure thresholds at 1 GiB (warning) and 2 GiB (critical) — values that were reasonable for Node's default `--max-old-space-size` (~2 GB server / ~4 GB desktop) but do not scale when operators configure a larger heap limit.

This change derives default heap warning and critical thresholds from V8's effective `heap_size_limit`, so they automatically adapt to whatever `--max-old-space-size` is set:

- **Critical**: 75% of the V8 heap limit, floored at 2 GiB
- **Warning**: 60% of the V8 heap limit, floored at 1 GiB

The conservative lower bounds ensure small-heap or default-heap environments remain equally protected. RSS threshold and RSS growth detection are unchanged. No configuration key is added — the fix is fully automatic.

## User Impact

Users on decently-provisioned hosts (e.g. `--max-old-space-size=8192`) no longer see spurious `heap_threshold` critical pressure from routine heap usage at 2 GB, while the same protection level is preserved for default or constrained heap sizes. The change is invisible to operators: no new config, no migration, no restart requirement beyond the usual update.

## Evidence

### Unit tests

3 new focused tests, 14 total, all passing (99 tests across 3 diagnostic suites):

| Test | What it proves |
|------|---------------|
| `default heap thresholds never go below the original constants as a conservative lower bound (#104631)` | Adaptive defaults floor at 1 GiB / 2 GiB — small-heap protection unchanged |
| `emits heap_threshold at the adaptive default warning threshold (#104631)` | Warning fires at 60% of the real V8 `heap_size_limit` |
| `emits heap_threshold critical at the adaptive default critical threshold (#104631)` | Critical fires at 75% of the real V8 `heap_size_limit` |

All tests call the exported `emitDiagnosticMemorySample()` without a `thresholds` override, exercising the real default path that the gateway heartbeat uses.

### Real-behavior proof

A standalone harness exercises the production adaptive-threshold computation and real `process.memoryUsage()` sampling across three isolated subprocesses with different `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size` configurations. Each subprocess calls `v8.getHeapStatistics()` and `process.memoryUsage()` — the same APIs the gateway heartbeat uses — and reports the computed thresholds and current memory state.

**Default V8 heap limit (~4.19 GB):**
```
limit=4.19 GB  w=2.51 GB  c=3.14 GB
heap=0.00 GB  => none
floor_warning=PASS (1.00 GB)  floor_critical=PASS (2.00 GB)
2.5 GB heap: old=critical/hardcoded_2GB  new=no (adaptive 3.14 GB)
```
The 2.5 GB heap case that would have triggered critical under the old hardcoded threshold is now correctly classified as no pressure.

**Enlarged heap (max-old-space-size=8192, matching reporter's ~8 GB environment):**
```
limit=8.19 GB  w=4.91 GB  c=6.14 GB
heap=0.00 GB  => none
floor_warning=PASS (1.00 GB)  floor_critical=PASS (2.00 GB)
2.5 GB heap: old=critical/hardcoded_2GB  new=no (adaptive 6.14 GB)
```
The false-positive critical at 2 GB is eliminated. The adaptive threshold correctly scales to 6.14 GB.

**Constrained heap (max-old-space-size=1024, ~1.19 GB):**
```
limit=1.19 GB  w=1.00 GB  c=2.00 GB
heap=0.00 GB  => none
floor_warning=PASS (1.00 GB)  floor_critical=PASS (2.00 GB)
2.5 GB heap: old=critical/hardcoded_2GB  new=yes
```
The conservative floor ensures thresholds never drop below the original 1 GiB / 2 GiB safety net.

**Typecheck**: `tsgo:core` passes clean.

**Lint**: `oxlint` zero errors.

**98 existing tests** in the diagnostic logging suite remain green (no collateral damage).

---

This PR is AI-assisted. Analysis, implementation, and testing were performed using AI tools (opencode) with review by the author.

target.title: fix(webchat): preserve session context on first send after page load (#96331)
target.body: ## Summary WebChat `chat.send` now preserves session context on the first send after page load by passing the WebChat-backed `backingSessionId` as `CallerSessionId` through `MsgContext`, allowing `initSessionState` to trust the caller-verified session and skip freshness evaluation when the ID matches the store entry AND the entry is stale. This closes the gap where `chat.history` displayed full history but `chat.send` lost model-visible context after gateway restart. - **Problem**: `chat.history` reads the transcript directly from disk and displays full history, but `chat.send` independently evaluates session freshness via `initSessionState` and mints a new session when the existing one is stale (daily reset / idle expiry). After gateway restart or crossing the 4 AM daily reset boundary, the model responds without prior context even though history is visible. - **Solution**: The gateway `chat.send` handler already has `backingSessionId` from the WebChat client. Pass it as `CallerSessionId` in the `MsgContext`. In `initSessionState`, add a `callerVerifiedSession` guard — when the caller has already validated the session entry, the IDs match, AND the entry is stale (`entryFreshness?.fresh === false`), skip freshness evaluation and reuse the existing session. The `entryFreshness?.fresh === false` check makes this naturally one-shot: after the first successful send updates the session timestamp, subsequent sends go through normal freshness evaluation. `/new` and `/reset` always take precedence via the `!isNewSession` guard. Mismatched IDs fall through to normal freshness evaluation. - **What changed**: `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts` (+1: pass `CallerSessionId: backingSessionId`), `src/auto-reply/templating.ts` (+10: add `CallerSessionId` field to `MsgContext` type), `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts` (+16: add `callerVerifiedSession` guard to `freshEntry` computation, placed before `lockedModelSelection` to preserve existing guard priority), `src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts` (+268: 8 regression tests covering all guard paths including one-shot proof) - **What did NOT change**: Backend session init (`session.ts` existing freshness logic), gateway dispatch (`chat.ts` except one line), `MsgContext` type except the new optional field, plugin SDK exports, config, migration paths, `/new` and `/reset` behavior, heartbeat/system events, `reconnectResumeRequested` path, `lockedModelSelection` guard (preserved as-is in the `freshEntry` chain) ## Change Type & Scope ### Change Type - [x] Bug fix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Docs - [ ] Security hardening - [ ] Chore/infra ### Scope - [x] Gateway / orchestration - [ ] Skills / tool execution - [ ] Auth / tokens - [ ] Memory / storage - [ ] Integrations - [ ] API / contracts - [x] UI / DX - [ ] CI/CD / infra ## Linked Issue - Closes #96331 - [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression ## Motivation Web UI users returning to a chat session after gateway restart (most commonly noticed the next morning after the 4 AM daily reset boundary) would see their full chat history displayed correctly via `chat.history`, but the model would respond as if it had no prior context. The root cause was that `chat.history` reads the transcript directly from disk without freshness evaluation, while `chat.send` independently evaluates freshness via `initSessionState` and mints a new session when stale — the two paths disagreed on whether the session was valid. The fix is gateway-side, not UI-side: the `chat.send` handler already has `backingSessionId` from the WebChat client. By passing it through `MsgContext` as a caller-verified signal, `initSessionState` can trust the caller's session validation when the IDs match, without changing any freshness policy. ## Review Contract ```text Ref: #96331 / PR #96391 Surface: Gateway / session init / chat.send dispatch / MsgContext type Bug: chat.history shows session history but chat.send loses it after gateway restart Cause: chat.history reads transcript directly from disk (no freshness check) while chat.send independently evaluates freshness via initSessionState and mints a new sessionId when stale. The two paths disagreed on session validity. (src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts:689-712, src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts:4686) Confidence: confirmed by code analysis + reproducible scenario Provenance: introduced by: PR #89017 (added reconnectResumeRequested infrastructure but only for WebSocket reconnect, not fresh page load) made visible by: gateway restart + daily reset boundary crossing Confidence: clear Best fix: Yes. The gateway chat.send handler already has backingSessionId from the WebChat client. Adding one field to MsgContext and one guard to freshEntry is the minimal correct fix. The callerVerifiedSession guard sits before lockedModelSelection in the freshEntry OR chain, preserving all existing guards (isSystemEvent, reconnectResumeRequested, recoverTerminalVisibleEntry, softResetAllowed) without modifying any of them. The entryFreshness?.fresh === false check makes the bypass naturally one-shot — it only activates for truly stale sessions. Refactor: No — existing backend infrastructure is unchanged and sufficient. Proof: 149 session tests + 2 gateway chat tests pass (8 new), see test output below. Risk: Low. The guard requires FIVE conditions: !isNewSession, non-empty CallerSessionId string, canReuseExistingEntry, entry?.sessionId === ctx.CallerSessionId, AND entryFreshness?.fresh === false. All five must pass. The freshness check makes this naturally one-shot. Mismatch falls through to normal evaluation. /new and /reset always win. Heartbeat uses isSystemEvent (separate guard). The CallerSessionId field is optional on MsgContext — no existing callers are affected. ``` ## Real Behavior Proof **Behavior addressed**: Web UI `chat.history` displays full history but `chat.send` reaches model without context after gateway restart. After fix: `chat.send` carries `CallerSessionId`, `initSessionState` skips freshness evaluation when IDs match AND session is stale, model receives full context. **Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112-2.el8.x86_64, Node 22.19+, branch `fix/webchat-session-context-restart-96331`, rebased on upstream/main (`dfa580e9895`) **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: ```bash # Session tests — full regression suite pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts --run ``` ``` Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 149 passed (149) ``` ```bash # Gateway chat.send tests pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/chat.send-deleted-agent.test.ts --run ``` ``` Test Files 2 passed (2) Tests 2 passed (2) ``` **Evidence after fix**: Total: 151 tests passed across 3 test files, 0 regressions. New test coverage matrix (8 new tests): ``` Test scenario => Expected CallerSessionId matches daily-stale entry => isNewSession=false, session reused CallerSessionId matches idle-stale entry => isNewSession=false, session reused CallerSessionId with /new command => isNewSession=true, reset triggered CallerSessionId mismatches store entry => isNewSession=true, falls through CallerSessionId set but no store entry exists => isNewSession=true CallerSessionId is empty string => isNewSession=true, guard blocked Heartbeat without CallerSessionId (isSystemEvent guard) => isNewSession=false, independent path CallerSessionId matches fresh session (one-shot proof) => isNewSession=false, normal freshness ``` **Observed result after fix**: - `CallerSessionId: backingSessionId` is passed in every `chat.send` MsgContext - `callerVerifiedSession` guard activates when: `!isNewSession` AND non-empty `CallerSessionId` string AND `canReuseExistingEntry` AND `entry.sessionId === ctx.CallerSessionId` AND `entryFreshness?.fresh === false` - All five conditions must pass — no single condition can bypass freshness - The `entryFreshness?.fresh === false` check makes the bypass naturally one-shot: after the first successful send updates the session timestamp, subsequent sends go through normal freshness evaluation - `callerVerifiedSession` sits before `lockedModelSelection` in the `freshEntry` OR chain to preserve existing guard priority - `/new` and `/reset` always win via the `!isNewSession` guard - Heartbeat system events continue through independent `isSystemEvent` guard - `reconnectResumeRequested` path is unchanged - `recoverTerminalVisibleEntry` path is unchanged - `lockedModelSelection` guard is unchanged - All 149 existing session tests pass — zero regressions **What was not tested**: - Multi-tab Web UI scenarios with different sessions - Rapid page reload + send race conditions ### Environment - OS: Linux 4.19.112-2.el8.x86_64 - Runtime: Node 22.19+ - Branch: `fix/webchat-session-context-restart-96331` ## Conflicts Resolved Rebased onto `origin/main` (`dfa580e9895`). Resolved merge conflict in `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts`: the `freshEntry` computation had gained a new `(lockedModelSelection && canReuseExistingEntry) ||` guard upstream. The `callerVerifiedSession` guard was placed before `lockedModelSelection` in the OR chain so it takes priority when the caller has already verified the session. All existing guards are preserved without modification. Also picked up `b575b5ee9b1` which fixes a `gateway-protocol` type import in `server-chat.ts` that was failing CI builds. ## Risks and Mitigations - **Highest risk area**: The `callerVerifiedSession` guard skips freshness evaluation when `CallerSessionId` matches AND the entry is stale. If the WebChat client passes a stale/incorrect `backingSessionId`, the guard could match a truly-expired session. Mitigation: the session ID MUST match exactly (`entry.sessionId === ctx.CallerSessionId`), the entry MUST be stale (`entryFreshness?.fresh === false`), and `canReuseExistingEntry` must be true (entry exists, not force-new). The freshness check makes the bypass one-shot — it cannot permanently suppress configured reset policy. - **Compatibility impact**: None. `CallerSessionId` is an optional field on `MsgContext`. Existing callers (bots, cron, integrations) never set it, so they follow the same freshness path as before. ## Security Impact - [x] New permissions/capabilities? No - [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No - [x] New/changed network calls? No - [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No - [x] Data access scope changed? No ## Compatibility / Migration - [x] Backward compatible? Yes — optional field on MsgContext, all existing callers unaffected - [x] Config/env changes? No - [x] Migration needed? No ## Human Verification - **Verified scenarios**: ### Step 1: Open Web UI Open **http://127.0.0.1:18788/** in your browser ### Step 2: Build a conversation with context 1. Start a new chat in the Web UI 2. Send several meaningful messages 3. Confirm the model correctly responds and references prior context across 3-4 turns ### Step 3: Restart the gateway (trigger the bug) ```bash # Kill the current gateway kill $(pgrep -f "run-node.mjs.*gateway") ``` ```bash # Wait 2 seconds then restart sleep 2 OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1 nohup node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway > /tmp/openclaw-gateway.log 2>&1 & ``` ### Step 4: Verify the fix 1. Reopen/refresh the Web UI and navigate back to the **same** chat session 2. **Verify chat.history first**: the UI should display the full conversation history from before restart (all prior messages visible on the page) 3. **Verify chat.send**: send a new message referencing the prior conversation 4. Observe the model's response - **Edge cases checked**: Empty `currentSessionId` (no-op), mismatched session IDs (backend fallthrough), heartbeat events (independent isSystemEvent guard) - **What you did NOT verify**: Multi-tab scenarios, rapid reload + send races ## AI Assistance 🤖 - **AI-assisted**: Yes - **Co-Authored-By**: Claude - **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes - **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Issue #96331 analysis → identified gap between chat.history and chat.send session resolution → designed CallerSessionId propagation fix reusing existing MsgContext infrastructure and initSessionState guard pattern → squashed 3 commits into 1, rebased onto latest main, resolved `lockedModelSelection` conflict, picked up `b575b5ee9b1` type import fix ## Review Conversations - [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR. - [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment. Closes #96331 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

target.title: fix(memory-search): stop hybrid fusion from discounting vector-only multimodal results
target.body:
## Summary

Hybrid memory search ranks results with `finalScore = vectorWeight * vectorScore + textWeight * textScore`. `mergeHybridResults` (`extensions/memory-core/src/memory/hybrid.ts`) applied that formula uniformly to every candidate. Image and audio chunks only carry a synthetic label as text, e.g. `Image file: media/IMG_0007.png` (`buildMemoryMultimodalLabel`, `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/multimodal.ts`). A natural-language query shares no words with that label, so a media chunk's BM25/text score is structurally near zero and it is seeded into the merge with `textScore: 0`. Under the default `0.7` vector / `0.3` text weights, a semantically strong media match is scaled to 70% of its vector score and ranks below a weaker text chunk that matches query keywords.

The fix makes fusion modality-aware. `mergeHybridResults` keeps the established weighted formula for every candidate, and only for a vector-only classified media chunk does it collapse the score to the vector signal:

```diff
-    const score = params.vectorWeight * entry.vectorScore + params.textWeight * entry.textScore;
+    const dropMediaTextSignal =
+      entry.hasVector &&
+      !entry.hasKeyword &&
+      params.vectorWeight > 0 &&
+      params.isNonTextMediaPath?.(entry.path) === true;
+    const contentScore = dropMediaTextSignal
+      ? entry.vectorScore
+      : params.vectorWeight * entry.vectorScore + params.textWeight * keywordScore;
```

For a non-text media chunk that has only a vector signal, dropping the near-zero text weight and renormalizing by the remaining vector weight collapses the score to its vector score, on the same `[0,1]` scale as text candidates. Every other candidate keeps the exact established weighted formula, so scoring scale, `minScore` filtering, and result ordering outside the vector-only media case are unchanged, including for custom weights that do not sum to one.

The manager supplies the predicate from the already-known file path, reusing the classifier the sync path uses (`extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.ts`):

```ts
isNonTextMediaPath: (path) =>
  classifyMemoryMultimodalPath(path, this.settings.multimodal) !== null,
```

`classifyMemoryMultimodalPath` returns `null` when multimodal search is disabled, so the predicate is `false` for every path and behavior is identical to today on text-only setups. Modality is derived, not persisted, so there is no schema change or migration.

### Keyword-only media is preserved (review follow-up)

The first revision dropped the text weight for any media path. That zeroed a media chunk matched only by keyword (its label tokens) and no vector signal: `(0.7*0 + 0*text)/0.7 = 0`, dropping it from results. The merge now tracks an explicit `hasVector` flag per candidate and only drops the synthetic-label text signal when the candidate also has a vector signal. A keyword-only media hit keeps its normal text-weighted score, matching pre-fix behavior. Covered by a new regression test.

### Zero vector-weight configuration preserved (re-review follow-up)

`vectorWeight` may legitimately be `0` (existing memory tests run `{ vectorWeight: 0, textWeight: 1 }`). If a classified media chunk appeared in both the vector and keyword result sets, `hasVector` made the previous revision drop `textWeight`; `weightSum` then became `0 + 0` and the candidate scored `0`, suppressing a valid keyword match. The drop is also gated on a positive configured vector weight, so when `vectorWeight` is `0` the synthetic text signal is never the only meaningful signal and is kept. Covered by a regression test for a media candidate present in both result sets under `vectorWeight 0, textWeight 1`.

### Both-signal media keeps its real keyword score (re-review follow-up)

Media labels are indexed and searchable (a manager test expects `search("image")`/`search("audio")` to find media). So a user who searches the label or filename can get the same media chunk back from FTS and from vector search at once. Gating the drop only on `hasVector` discarded the BM25/text score for that both-signal case, ignoring a real keyword match under positive `vectorWeight` and down-ranking a media file that legitimately matched FTS. The drop is now also gated on the candidate having no keyword signal, so the synthetic-label text weight is dropped only for genuinely vector-only media:

```diff
     const dropMediaTextSignal =
       entry.hasVector &&
+      !entry.hasKeyword &&
       params.vectorWeight > 0 &&
       params.isNonTextMediaPath?.(entry.path) === true;
```

`hasKeyword` is tracked the same way as `hasVector`: it is set when a candidate is present in the keyword (FTS) result set. A vector-only media chunk (the #44540 case) still drops the synthetic label and scores on its vector signal; a media chunk with a real FTS hit now keeps the keyword contribution. Covered by a new regression test for a media candidate present in both result sets under positive vector weight.

### Normalization limited to vector-only classified media (re-review follow-up)

An earlier revision computed `contentScore = weighted / weightSum` for every candidate. `weightSum` equals `1` only when the configured weights already sum to one; the public config exposes `vectorWeight` and `textWeight` independently, and existing tests run `{ vectorWeight: 1, textWeight: 1 }`. Under such a configuration the division halved the score of ordinary text and vector-only non-media candidates, which could change ordering and `minScore` filtering outside the reported bug. The renormalization is now applied only when `dropMediaTextSignal` is true; every other candidate retains the established unnormalized weighted formula exactly:

```diff
-    const effectiveTextWeight = dropMediaTextSignal ? 0 : params.textWeight;
-    const weightSum = params.vectorWeight + effectiveTextWeight;
-    const weighted =
-      params.vectorWeight * entry.vectorScore + effectiveTextWeight * keywordScore;
-    const contentScore = weightSum > 0 ? weighted / weightSum : 0;
+    const contentScore = dropMediaTextSignal
+      ? entry.vectorScore
+      : params.vectorWeight * entry.vectorScore + params.textWeight * keywordScore;
```

Because `dropMediaTextSignal` is gated on `params.vectorWeight > 0`, collapsing the media score to `entry.vectorScore` is exactly `(vectorWeight * vectorScore) / vectorWeight` with no division by zero. Covered by two new regression tests, using `vectorWeight 1, textWeight 1` (weights that do not sum to one): a vector-only non-media candidate and a both-signal non-media candidate each keep the established weighted score.

What is intentionally out of scope: persisting a modality column on chunks, and any change to the text-only ranking path.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: hybrid fusion discounted vector-only image/audio matches by the configured text weight, so a semantically strong media result ranked below a weaker keyword-matching text result.
Real environment tested: a real `MemoryIndexManager` running the full pipeline (SQLite store, FTS5/BM25 keyword index, vector store, modality classification, hybrid fusion). Indexed a real image file plus a text note that keyword-matches the query, plus 18 filler text docs so BM25 has real IDF. Query `underwater coral reef survey`; the query embedding is aligned with the image vector while sharing no words with the `Image file:` label (so the image is a strong semantic match with `textScore 0`, exactly the reported case). Embeddings are a deterministic local stub (no Gemini key in this environment); the indexing, FTS/BM25, vector scoring, and fusion are the real code paths.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: ran the scenario through `MemoryIndexManager.search` with the patch, then swapped `hybrid.ts` for the `origin/main` version (isolated vitest module cache per run) and re-ran the identical scenario.
Evidence after fix:
```
BEFORE (origin/main):
  #1  score=0.9396  vec=0.9487  text=0.9186  field-notes.md   <- keyword-matching text note wins
  ...  IMG_0007.png discounted to score=0.7000 (vec=1.0000, text=0.0000), tied with filler docs, buried
  => top result: field-notes.md

AFTER (patch):
  #1  score=1.0000  vec=1.0000  text=0.0000  IMG_0007.png      <- strongest semantic match now surfaces
  #2  score=0.9396  vec=0.9487  text=0.9186  field-notes.md
  => top result: IMG_0007.png
```
Observed result after fix: the image is renormalized to its vector score (1.0) and ranks first; the text note keeps its identical score (0.9396) and the rank order flips so the most semantically relevant media result surfaces.
What was not tested: a live Gemini-keyed embedding backend end-to-end (no API key available in this environment); embeddings were a deterministic stub while every retrieval/fusion path was real.
Proof limitations or environment constraints: the corpus is synthetic (1 image, 1 keyword-matching note, 18 filler docs) to give BM25 meaningful IDF; the throwaway proof tests are not committed.

### Additional runtime evidence: both-signal media keyword score (re-review follow-up)

Drove the real production fusion `mergeHybridResults` with the real `classifyMemoryMultimodalPath` predicate (image modality enabled) for a classified image present in BOTH the vector and keyword result sets under the default `vectorWeight 0.7, textWeight 0.3`, alongside a competing text note. `classifyMemoryMultimodalPath("memory/generated/images/diagram.png")` returns `image`; `"memory/notes.md"` returns `null`. The image carries a real FTS/BM25 hit (`text=0.95`, e.g. the user searched the filename `diagram`). Compared the head ClawSweeper reviewed (`3220af91bf`) against this patch (isolated vitest module cache per side):

```
BEFORE (3220af91bf):
  memory/notes.md                          score=0.7040 vec=0.6200 text=0.9000
  memory/generated/images/diagram.png      score=0.6200 vec=0.6200 text=0.9500  <- real FTS hit dropped
  => top result: memory/notes.md

AFTER (this patch):
  memory/generated/images/diagram.png      score=0.7190 vec=0.6200 text=0.9500  <- keyword match counts
  memory/notes.md                          score=0.7040 vec=0.6200 text=0.9000
  => top result: memory/generated/images/diagram.png
```

The media chunk's genuine keyword match was being discarded (score collapsed to its vector-only `0.62`, ranked below the weaker text note); it now keeps the BM25 contribution (`0.719`) and the rank flips so the media file that actually matched FTS surfaces first. The vector-only #44540 behavior and the zero-vector-weight behavior are both unchanged.

### Additional runtime evidence: non-media scoring under weights that do not sum to one (re-review follow-up)

Drove the real production fusion `mergeHybridResults` with `vectorWeight 1, textWeight 1` (weights that do not sum to one) for non-media candidates plus a vector-only classified media candidate, comparing the previously reviewed head (`fa443f4b28`, over-broad normalization) against this patch (isolated vitest module cache per side):

```
BEFORE (fa443f4b28, over-broad normalization):
  non-media vector-only (weights 1/1): score=0.3    <- established score 0.6 halved by /weightSum
  non-media both-signal (weights 1/1): score=0.75   <- established score 1.5 halved by /weightSum
  vector-only media     (weights 1/1): score=0.6

AFTER (this patch):
  non-media vector-only (weights 1/1): score=0.6    <- established weighted formula preserved
  non-media both-signal (weights 1/1): score=1.5    <- established weighted formula preserved
  vector-only media     (weights 1/1): score=0.6    <- #44540 collapse to vector signal unchanged
```

Non-media candidates are no longer rescaled by `weightSum`, so their scores, `minScore` filtering, and ordering are unchanged under custom weights; the vector-only media collapse targeted by #44540 is preserved.

## Verification

- Real before/after through `MemoryIndexManager.search` above (full SQLite + FTS5/BM25 + vector + fusion), `origin/main` vs patch with isolated vitest module caches.
- Real before/after through the production `mergeHybridResults` + real `classifyMemoryMultimodalPath` for the both-signal media case (`3220af91bf` vs this patch), showing the dropped keyword score restored and the rank flip.
- Real before/after through the production `mergeHybridResults` for non-media candidates under `vectorWeight 1, textWeight 1` (`fa443f4b28` vs this patch), showing the established score preserved instead of halved.
- Added regression coverage in `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/hybrid.test.ts`: vector-only media scored on its vector signal without the text-weight discount; text-candidate scoring unchanged when a media predicate is supplied; keyword-only media preserved (not dropped to zero); a classified media candidate present in both result sets under `vectorWeight 0, textWeight 1` keeps its keyword score; a classified media candidate present in both result sets under positive vector weight keeps its keyword score instead of being discounted; and, under `vectorWeight 1, textWeight 1`, a vector-only non-media candidate and a both-signal non-media candidate each keep the established weighted score.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/memory/hybrid.test.ts` (22 passed).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search.test.ts` (34 passed).
- `tsgo` extensions typecheck passes; oxlint clean on the changed files.

Closes #44540

target.title: fix(compaction): emit after_compaction on no-op and use JSON-safe validator delimiters (#81925)
target.body:
## Summary

OpenClaw issue #81925 documents two coupled defects that surface as HTTP 500s on voice channels when the context engine runs under memory pressure, especially for open-weight tool-calling models:

1. `after_compaction` is never emitted when compaction is a legitimate no-op (`{ok:true, compacted:false}`), so plugin observers that pair `before_compaction`/`after_compaction` wait forever and time out.
2. Schema-validation error messages wrap property names in single quotes (`'sessionTarget'`). Models trained on JSON tool calls copy the trailing `'` delimiter back into their next attempt and get stuck in an unrecoverable retry loop.

This change fixes both, on every surface where they occur, and updates the internal callers that pattern-match those validator messages so the delimiter change does not break cross-version behavior.

## Root cause

### Bug 1: after_compaction not emitted on no-op compaction

`before_compaction` fires unconditionally once the engine owns compaction, but `after_compaction` was gated on `result.compacted === true` on **three** independent compaction surfaces:

- `compact.queued.ts` (engine-owned queued path): the after-hook block required `result.ok && result.compacted`.
- `compact.ts` `compactEmbeddedAgentSessionDirect` (native direct path): the `!containsRealConversationMessages(...)` early return sent `{ok:true, compacted:false, reason:"no real conversation messages"}` straight back to the caller, after `before_compaction` already fired, without ever calling `runAfterCompactionHooks`.
- `run.ts` `runOwnsCompactionAfterHook` (timeout-recovery and overflow-recovery paths): paired with `runOwnsCompactionBeforeHook`, which fires `before_compaction` unconditionally, but the after-hook returned early on `!compactResult.compacted`.

So a paired observer sees `before` with no matching `after`. The voice plugin waits out its 3s timeout, falls back to `tool-result-truncation`, and only recovers after ~3 attempts (~2.5 min), long after the client has already 500'd.

### Bug 2: validator delimiters trip tool callers

Validation error formatting wrapped property names in single quotes in two places:

- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/validation-errors.ts` `formatValidationErrors`: `unexpected property '<name>'` and `must have required property '<name>'` (gateway RPC params + plugin session action result validation, the surface an LLM-driven action call hits).
- `src/plugins/schema-validator.ts` `formatRequiredMessage`: `must have required property '<name>'` (plugin session action **payload** validation, the surface an LLM-submitted payload hits). Its sibling `additionalProperties` message was already double-quoted, so this was the lone single-quote holdout.

A model that parses the error and copies the property token captures `<name>'` (with the stray quote), re-emits the same malformed key, and re-triggers the identical error.

### Bug 2 follow-through: version-fallback detectors keyed on the old wording

Several internal callers strip an additive request field and retry when an **older** gateway rejects it, and they recognize that rejection by matching the validator's `unexpected property '<name>'` text. Switching the producer to `JSON.stringify` (double-quoted) would make those single-quote matchers silently stop recognizing a newer gateway's rejection, quietly breaking the mixed-version fallback the matchers exist to provide. Five such detectors match this wording: `cron-tool.ts` (`cron.list` compact), `gateway.ts` (`connect` identity-token and `node.invoke` turn-source), `sessions-resolution.ts` (`sessions.resolve` allowMissing), and `ui/src/lib/sessions/usage.ts` (`sessions.usage` timeZone).

## Fix

- **Bug 1, all three surfaces:** emit `after_compaction` whenever compaction completes (`result.ok`), with `compactedCount: 0` and a `reason` discriminator on the no-op path. The engine paths forward the engine's own skip reason (default `policy_skipped`); the native path reports `no_real_conversation_messages`. Added an optional `reason?: string` to the `after_compaction` hook contract (`PluginHookAfterCompactionEvent`, `CompactionHookRunner`, `runAfterCompactionHooks`), additive and backward compatible. The `!compactResult.ok` guard is preserved, so genuine failures/aborts still do not emit a success `after_compaction`.
- **Bug 2, all four property-name branches:** format every property name through `JSON.stringify(name)` rather than interpolating it into hand-written quotes. This covers `unexpected property` and `must have required property` in `formatValidationErrors`, and `must have required property` plus the `additionalProperties` list in `schema-validator`. `JSON.stringify` emits a real JSON string token, so the delimiter matches JSON tool-call syntax **and** a name that itself contains a `"`, `\`, or control character is properly escaped. A model that copies the token back always gets a clean, parseable JSON key.
- **Detectors, all five surfaces:** add one shared `messageReportsUnexpectedProperty(message, name)` helper co-located with the producer in `validation-errors.ts` that accepts both the legacy single-quoted and the new `JSON.stringify` wording, and route every version-fallback detector through it. The mirror of `JSON.stringify` on both the producer and the matcher keeps the escaping symmetric. `context-engine/registry.ts` already matched single, double, and backtick quotes, so it needed no change.

## Why this covers the whole issue (not one surface)

- The no-op `after_compaction` gap existed on **three** independent compaction code paths (engine-owned queued, native direct, and timeout/overflow recovery). Fixing only one would still hang on the others. All three are fixed and all three have regression coverage.
- The delimiter/escaping issue existed across **four** property-name branches on **two** independent validator paths. All four now route through `JSON.stringify`.
- The delimiter change would otherwise regress **five** version-fallback detectors that recognize an older gateway by the old wording. All five now accept both wordings through one shared matcher, so mixed-version `cron.list`, `connect`, `node.invoke`, `sessions.resolve`, and `sessions.usage` fallbacks keep firing, and each has both-wording retry coverage.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.hooks.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.timeout-triggered-compaction.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.overflow-compaction.test.ts` -> compaction regression coverage passing (engine-skip no-op, engine default reason, native-skip paired-observer, timeout-recovery no-op, overflow-recovery no-op).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts` -> 56 passed (adds the `messageReportsUnexpectedProperty` unit coverage plus the JSON-token validator assertions).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts src/agents/tools/gateway.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-resolution.test.ts` -> 223 passed (each version-fallback detector now parametrized over both wordings).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/lib/sessions/usage.test.ts` -> 5 passed (`sessions.usage` retry parametrized over both wordings).

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: a no-op compaction now emits `after_compaction` (so a paired voice observer is not left waiting); both validators now format property names through `JSON.stringify` (so a tool-calling model always copies back a valid, parseable JSON key even when the property name contains a `"` or `\`); and every version-fallback detector that recognizes an older gateway rejecting an additive field now accepts both the legacy single-quoted and the new JSON-quoted wording, so the delimiter change does not silently break mixed-version fallbacks.

Real environment tested: the actual built-from-source OpenClaw runtime functions in this branch, driven directly through `node` (via the `tsx` ESM loader) outside any harness. Bug 1 drives the real `containsRealConversationMessages`, `runBeforeCompactionHooks`, and `runAfterCompactionHooks` from `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/`, with a real `registerInternalHook` voice-style observer. Bug 2 drives the real `formatValidationErrors` from `packages/gateway-protocol/` and the real `validateJsonSchemaValue` from `src/plugins/schema-validator.ts`. The detector proof drives the real shared `messageReportsUnexpectedProperty` and the real `requestSessionsUsage` retry path from `ui/src/lib/sessions/usage.ts`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: register a paired `session:compact:before` / `session:compact:after` observer, feed a heartbeat-only transcript (so `containsRealConversationMessages` returns false, the real no-op trigger), then run the real before/after emission the patched no-op branch performs; feed a hostile property name containing an embedded quote and backslash into the real gateway-protocol formatter and the real plugin schema-validator, read back each formatted message, and parse the token a JSON model would copy back; then take the patched formatter's own JSON-quoted rejection, run it through both the old single-quoted matching form and the new shared matcher, and drive the real `requestSessionsUsage` against a gateway that rejects the additive `timeZone` field in each wording to observe whether the additive field is stripped and the call retried.

Evidence after fix (live console output from `node` driving the real runtime functions):

```
$ node --import tsx proof-bug1.mts   # drives real compaction hook emission
containsRealConversationMessages(heartbeat) = false

# BEFORE the fix (no-op fires before_compaction only):
  observer pending balance = 1 <- stuck, after_compaction never arrives (hang)
  observer received after  = null

# AFTER the fix (no-op also fires after_compaction):
  observer pending balance = 0 <- balanced
  observer received after  = {"compactedCount":0,"reason":"no_real_conversation_messages"}

$ node --import tsx proof-validator-escape.mts   # drives real validators
property name a hostile schema/model supplies: "evil\"key\\path"

# BEFORE (raw interpolation into hand-written double quotes):
  message = "at root: unexpected property \"evil\"key\\path\""
  token a model copies = "\"evil\"key\\path\""
  copies as a clean JSON key? = false

# AFTER (real gateway-protocol formatValidationErrors):
  message = "at root: unexpected property \"evil\\\"key\\\\path\""
  copies as a clean JSON key? = true

# AFTER (real plugin schema-validator required-property miss):
  message = "must have required property \"evil\\\"key\\\\path\""
  contains a valid JSON string token? = true

$ node --import tsx proof-detector.mts   # drives real matcher + requestSessionsUsage retry
patched producer message = "invalid sessions.usage params: at root: unexpected property \"timeZone\""

# BEFORE (shipped detector: single-quoted includes only):
  matches patched producer output? = false  <- version fallback silently stops firing

# AFTER (shared messageReportsUnexpectedProperty, both wordings):
  matches legacy single-quoted rejection? = true
  matches JSON-quoted rejection?          = true

# real requestSessionsUsage retry against an older gateway:
  legacy single-quoted rejection -> stripped timeZone, retried (calls=2)
  JSON-quoted rejection          -> stripped timeZone, retried (calls=2)
  unrelated invalid-usage error   -> rethrown, not retried
```

Observed result after fix: the real no-op path now delivers `after_compaction` with `{compactedCount:0, reason:"no_real_conversation_messages"}` to the paired observer, returning its pending balance to 0 instead of hanging at 1; for a property name carrying an embedded quote and backslash, both the real gateway-protocol formatter and the real plugin schema-validator now emit a `JSON.stringify`-escaped token that round-trips through `JSON.parse` back to the original name; and the version-fallback detectors now recognize the patched validator's JSON-quoted rejection that the shipped single-quoted matcher missed, so the real `requestSessionsUsage` strips the additive `timeZone` field and retries against an older gateway in both wordings, while an unrelated invalid-usage error is still rethrown without a retry.

What was not tested: a live end-to-end voice-channel session against a real 7B-14B llama-server under memory pressure. This change is at the compaction-hook, validation-formatter, and version-fallback-detector layers, exercised above by driving the real runtime functions plus the regression coverage; a full hardware voice loop was out of scope for this environment.

target.title: fix(browser): normalize geolocation permission origins
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users calling Browser `/set/geolocation` with a normal page URL in `origin`, such as `https://x.test/path`, did not get the same origin normalization as `/permissions/grant`, and malformed or `file://` origins were not rejected before the Playwright geolocation set path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Browser routes now share one HTTP(S) origin parser. `/set/geolocation` normalizes supplied origins to `URL.origin` before invoking Playwright and rejects non-HTTP(S) or malformed origins for geolocation set operations with the same error used by the dedicated permissions route.

The clear path intentionally returns before parsing `origin`, because clearing geolocation and permissions does not use an origin. This preserves existing clients that send stale or malformed origin fields while clearing state.

## User Impact

Users can pass page URLs as geolocation permission origins and get the expected site origin grant. Invalid local-file or malformed origins fail fast with a clear 400 response for set operations instead of reaching the browser mutation path. `clear=true` still clears geolocation even when an unused origin field is malformed.

## Evidence

Exact head: `4c82a884ebec97d3d4a22b79e072fdc9697a4c76`.

- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/permissions.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 2 files / 25 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/permissions.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/origin.ts` passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/permissions.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/origin.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Proof

- The route-level `/set/geolocation` proof exercises the registered Browser route handler with the Playwright geolocation adapter mocked at the plugin boundary.
- It proves a supplied page URL, `https://geo.example/path?query=1#hash`, is normalized before the adapter call, and Playwright receives `origin: "https://geo.example"`.
- It proves `file:///tmp/page.html` and malformed set origins return 400 before tab resolution and before any Playwright geolocation call.
- It proves `clear=true` returns before parsing unused coordinates or origin, so malformed unused origin input cannot block geolocation clearing; the adapter receives `clear: true` for the selected tab.
- The sibling `/permissions/grant` route proof remains in the focused run to show the shared HTTP(S) origin parser keeps permission-origin behavior aligned.

AI-assisted by Codex.

target.title: fix(microsoft-foundry): reject malformed endpoints
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Malformed Microsoft Foundry base URLs could be treated as usable endpoints. `extractFoundryEndpoint()` called `normalizeFoundryEndpoint()` directly, and the fallback normalization path returned a trimmed string even when `new URL(...)` could not parse the value.

## Why This Change Was Made

Runtime endpoint extraction should only accept real HTTP(S) URLs. When a configured model endpoint is malformed, the provider should ignore that unusable value and continue to the existing metadata or environment fallback path instead of building provider URLs from invalid text.

## User Impact

Users with stale or malformed Foundry model base URLs can still recover through valid Entra profile metadata or endpoint fallback sources. Invalid configured endpoint strings no longer block a working Foundry configuration from being used.

## Evidence

The regression test covers a model with `baseUrl: "not a url"` and valid Entra profile metadata. Before this change, endpoint extraction treated the malformed string as present; after this change it returns `undefined` and runtime auth builds the base URL from the metadata endpoint.

## Proof

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=.vitest-cache-foundry-endpoint node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/microsoft-foundry/index.test.ts`
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/microsoft-foundry/shared.ts extensions/microsoft-foundry/index.test.ts`
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint extensions/microsoft-foundry/shared.ts extensions/microsoft-foundry/index.test.ts`
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine claude`
